summary: Make budget the canonical TypeScript DSL admission metadata authoring surface

replay.detail: TypeScript authoring only. Native KDL output is byte-identical; stored declarations and replay interpretation are unchanged.

schema.detail: No storage schema, generated SDK, client-v0 schema, or native KDL wire-shape changes. The TypeScript DSL lowers canonical budget fields to the existing declared-priority, declared-lane and declared-budgets nodes.

rules.detail: The TypeScript DSL accepts admission metadata only through budget.scheduling and budget.resources. Retired declaredPriority, declaredLane and declaredBudgets authoring keys are refused, as are unknown keys at every budget level. Agents accept memoryMax and diskMax; missions additionally accept cpuSeconds and tokenBudget. Steps, loops and rounds have no budget. Native admission rules and KDL output are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: TypeScript authors using declaredPriority, declaredLane or declaredBudgets must migrate to budget. A local consumer scan found zero matches on factory main. Fractal has only historical compatibility documentation and release-note hits outside packages/fractal; dotfiles has only embedded historical diff substring matches for declaredLanes. No live consumer authoring hits were found in those scanned checkouts. Native KDL output is byte-identical.

downtime.detail: TypeScript authoring only; native KDL output is byte-identical. No service interruption, restart, migration or backfill is required by this change.

manual.detail: Migrate declaredPriority to budget.scheduling.priority, declaredLane to budget.scheduling.lane, and declaredBudgets to budget.resources. Move agent cpuSeconds and tokenBudget declarations to mission resources. Keep mission and step timeout top-level; do not add budget to steps, loops or rounds.

recovery.detail: Native KDL output is byte-identical and persisted declarations are unchanged. No data recovery, repricing, rollback migration or roll-forward migration is needed.
